the regulation of body sodium is accomplished by a complex interrelationship of several factors including the daily filtered load of sodium, the daily glomerular filtrate, the serum concentrations of the sodium salt, and the serum concentration of the anion of that salt.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the intrinsic renal mechanisms that participate in the regulation of sodium balance in normal and in abnormal subjects.
the mechanisms that regulate body sodium and potassium.
the mechanisms of electrolyte regulation in normal subjects and patients with renal disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the regulation of body sodium is a dynamic process that is not derived from adrenal steroid secretion and that is regulated in part through intrinsic renal mechanisms.
the renal excretory mechanism for sodium is more sensitive than that for potassium, and that the renal excretion of sodium is regulated by both intrinsic and hormonal factors.
the renal mechanisms for the control of body sodium are more complex than those for potassium, and that sodium excretion is more dependent on the volume of urine excreted.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
sodium balance is controlled through periodic variations in glomerular filtration, in the filtered load and in the excretory response to loading.
the regulation of body sodium and potassium balance is accomplished by intrinsic renal mechanisms which are not influenced by the adrenal steroids.
in normal man sodium balance is controlled in part by the kidney, and that the kidney is a major factor in the control of sodium balance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a daily cycle in the regulation of sodium balance in man.
the kidney has a remarkable ability to regulate the body's electrolyte composition, even without hormones.
the kidney is the primary organ for the regulation of electrolyte balance, and that the renal mechanisms for the control of electrolyte excretion are complex and involve many factors.
